# Pending changes (since patch 0005, 2026-11-08)

## 2026-11-08 - GUI redesign (1): one look after the reference console
- Asked: use the new reference image (~/Downloads/faae9bd1-...png - a "Thalassa sector" map console: dark teal
  glass panels, thin glowing cyan borders, orange for the active tab / highlights / corner trims, squared techno
  headings) as the template for the whole GUI; the GUI no longer changes with the empire's space; the illustrated
  map as the guide for planet maps; similar icons for the system and galaxy maps; icons redrawn to suit what they
  stand for; keep the colour theme and glow; the planet picture panel (top left) at the bottom right with the
  planet's name and description.
- Phase 1 (this entry) - the theme:
  - NeonTheme: one palette - CYAN (0.24, 0.86, 1.0), the highlight PINK is now orange (1.0, 0.52, 0.12), BG dark
    teal (0.012, 0.045, 0.06); text pale cyan. set_empire() keeps the neutral look whatever the empire (PALETTES
    kept for the GUI-look editor). Every pink/navy-tinted background now derives from the palette (hi_bg()).
  - Headings, tabs and big buttons: Rajdhani Bold (SIL OFL, assets/fonts/Rajdhani-{Bold,SemiBold}.ttf +
    Rajdhani-LICENSE.txt) instead of slanted Noto Black.
  - NeonBox: optional corner accents - glowing orange trims along the two cut corners (panels).
  - UI.panel_style: every code-built panel the same (cyan border, orange trims), whatever colour the caller asked;
    UI.tab_bar: the selected tab lit orange (the reference's MAP tab), the rest dark glass with a cyan edge, 20 px.
  - HUD / event log / toolbar / landing labels follow the palette (comments updated; two hard-coded backgrounds).
- Tests: test_gui.test_one_palette_everywhere replaces test_palette_per_empire.
- Files: scripts/neon_theme.gd, neon_box.gd, ui.gd, hud.gd, event_log.gd, toolbar.gd, landing_ui.gd, tests/test_gui.gd;
  new assets/fonts/Rajdhani-Bold.ttf, Rajdhani-SemiBold.ttf (+ .import), Rajdhani-LICENSE.txt

## 2026-11-08 - GUI redesign (2): the planet card
- The reference's sector panel (picture, label / value rows) as a planet card at the bottom right in space
  (scripts/planet_card.gd, new PlanetCard, added to the HUD by main.gd): the planet under the mouse, else the one
  you're within 900 of its edge; name (Rajdhani 26), kind (+ "moon of ..."), a 308 x 150 picture - a slice of the
  planet 1.5x the width, lit from the upper left, over stars, cyan frame with an orange tick - then SYSTEM, ORBIT,
  MOONS / PARENT, SURFACE, THREAT (orange when high) and the description. Fades in / out (0.25 s); checks every
  0.2 s; hidden in signal sites. 340 px wide, 16 px from the corner: clear of the toolbar and the event log.
- Files: new scripts/planet_card.gd; scripts/main.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Exhaust trails for every ship (after the reference sheet)
- Asked: a new reference image in Downloads (e3f9e630-...png: 80s-anime jets with blue, orange and magenta
  exhaust trails) as the template for exhaust trails on all NPC and player ships - long, but never covering the
  whole window, fading out with time; "stick as close as you can to that reference image".
- ExhaustTrail (scripts/exhaust_trail.gd, new): follows where the nozzle has been (world space; a point every
  9 px, the newest riding the nozzle), so turns leave curves. Drawn like the reference: billowing round puffs in
  three flat cel tones (a darker shade on one side, the body, a light band on the other - colour shifting from
  the nozzle colour to a deeper one far back), crackling lightning streaks (3, re-jagged every 4 frames, additive),
  a white-hot core for the first 28 %, and a plume at the nozzle (white core, coloured flame, glow). Puffs grow with
  age (x2.1 at the end of their life), taper to a thin curling tip; each puff lasts LIFE 1.6 s; length capped at
  5 x the ship's length (320-760 px - the player's ~580 px of a 1920 px window). Width 0.22 x length (11-50).
  Styles: blue (player; Athenians, Ionians), orange (pirates, Spartans, hostiles), magenta (Minoans, Mycenaeans,
  others); creatures have none. Off-screen trails aren't drawn. 60 fps with 16 trails (same as without).
- The player's old triangle flame is gone (Ship._draw) - the trail's plume replaces it.
- Tests: test_play's two "GUI theme follows the empire" checks now expect the one look.
- Files: new scripts/exhaust_trail.gd; scripts/ship.gd, scripts/enemy.gd, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-08 - GUI redesign (3): the planet map after the reference console
- The planet picture (PlanetSurface._map_color / _style_map_bytes, on the worker thread; _repaint_map for local
  terrain changes): deep navy sea with a faint grid every 44 tiles, shallows lighter; land dark teal tinted 42 %
  by its terrain colour, hillshaded from the broad slope (+-12 cells, light from the top: the steepest lit faces
  orange, the others darker); glowing cyan coastlines (1 cell bright, 2 cells faint). Landing still ~5.5 s.
- The planet map (SurfaceMap): a LAYERS panel (Routes, Places, People, Grid check boxes) on the left; the map
  draws a console grid and an oval frame ring; settlements (building groups within 40 tiles) as circled icons -
  a temple for the palace, a skyline for the others - with orange glowing routes from your ship to each and
  dotted cyan ones between them; your ship an orange pulsing badge, you a walking-figure badge, pirates red
  warning badges, citizens gold dots; a compass rose (N) and a scale bar (0 50 100 250 m); the planet card at the
  bottom right (SYSTEM, TERRAIN, SETTLEMENTS, EXPLORED, THREAT, description). Hovering a settlement names it;
  clicking walks there. PlanetCard.show_planet() fills a card by hand (also used by the space card).
- The minimap: buildings cyan-outlined teal, your ship orange.
- Docs: game.md (surface-map section: the new look and Layers; credits: the fonts).
- Files: scripts/planet_surface.gd, surface_map.gd, surface_minimap.gd, planet_card.gd, data/docs/game.md

## 2026-11-08 - GUI redesign (4): map icons for the system and galaxy maps; tab icons
- MapIcons (scripts/map_icons.gd, new): the console's markers - a glowing ring on dark glass with a line glyph
  (temple, city, ship, you, warning, pirate, mountain, star, planet, ringed, moon, station, gate, asteroid,
  signal, quest, trader) in cyan / orange / red; route() draws glowing or dotted routes with nodes.
- System map (pages/map_page.gd): the star a circled sun; planets keep their small shaded disc inside a cyan
  (orange: landable) ring, with a planet / ringed / moon badge; stations a station badge (hub, arms, solar
  wings); gates a portal badge; signals a pulsing signal badge; survey points a mountain badge; the objective a
  pulsing orange quest badge; ships small arrows pointing where they fly (red hostile, orange provoked, mint
  neutral); your ship an orange arrow in a ring and your course an orange glowing route; Rajdhani labels;
  legend recoloured.
- Galaxy map (pages/galaxy_page.gd): the console grid; systems circled stars ringed in the owner's colour;
  lanes dotted cyan (red dotted at war fronts); your planned route an orange glowing route; you an orange pulsing
  ring; the system-state arc orange.
- The Ship Computer's tabs got icons that say what each page is (EditorIcons ui_*: glowing line icons): Quest a
  journal, Inventory a cargo crate, Tech Tree a circuit tree, Encyclopedia an open book, Tutorial an info badge,
  Map a planet with its orbit and moon, Galaxy a spiral galaxy (were a flag, a shopping cart, a star, a book, a
  "?", a planet and a crosshair). EditorIcons' colours follow the GUI: BLUE -> the cyan, GOLD -> the orange.
- Files: new scripts/map_icons.gd; scripts/pages/map_page.gd, pages/galaxy_page.gd, editor_icons.gd, ship_menu.gd

## 2026-11-08 - 80s-anime look for the sprites
- Asked: use the reference's spaceships to stylise the existing ones without changing their designs - a bit of
  80s anime look for the game in general - and update the rest of the sprites to fit.
- tools/anime_style.py (new, numpy): per sprite - smooths fine surface noise inside the silhouette (60 %), cel
  shading (luminance snapped to 4 tones, 85 %), saturation x1.38, contrast x1.08, a bright rim along the edges
  facing the top-left light, a dark inner ink line and a bold navy outline (about 2.5 px at the size shown;
  max(2, size / 75) texture px). The untouched PNGs go to external/sprite_originals/ the first time (339 kept);
  data/sprites is always made from them (re-runs never compound; --restore puts them back).
- Styled: 73 ships, 24 stations, 2 citizens (99), and the 240 rig parts of the surface characters (no seams at the
  joints at play zoom). Tiles (buildings: they'd seam) and fx (glows) are left as they were.
- Tests: test_ionia's "Ionian GUI theme" check now expects the one look. Full suite: 104 passed, 1 (that check)
  failed before the fix; test_ionia 3/3 after.
- Files: new tools/anime_style.py; data/sprites/{ship,station,npc,rig}_*.png (339 restyled); tests/test_ionia.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Signal paths as glowing routes
- Asked: the paths to located signals (after a system scan) more like the glowing routes in the reference image,
  without the arrows.
- ShipScanner._draw_paths: each path is now a gentle curve (bowed 10 % of its length, alternate paths opposite
  ways) from just off your ship to the signal, drawn like the console's routes - a wide soft glow (34 px), a glow
  (14 px), a bright core (3.5 px) in the signal's colour, easing in from the ship; light nodes along it (5 per
  path); three pulses of light running out to the signal; glowing pulsing rings at the signal. Sizes are in
  screen pixels (they don't thin out when zoomed out). The chevrons and the dashes are gone. Still fades with
  the scan's arrows and is dropped when the scan ends.
- Files: scripts/ship_scanner.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Scanner animations in the same glowing style
- Asked: the scanner's animations in a style very like the glowing signal paths (the reference console).
- System scan (ShipScanner._draw_waves): each ring now a wide soft glow (40 px), a glow (14 px) and a bright core
  (3 px) with 12 light nodes turning round it, plus a radar sweep - a bright arm with a fading wedge behind it,
  growing with the rings, from an orange hub at the ship; fades with the scan.
- Asteroid scan (_draw_rock_scan): the beam is a glowing route (22 / 9 / 2.5 px) with three light pulses running
  to where it touches; a glowing scan line over the rock; glowing target rings with 6 turning nodes; an orange
  progress arc filling round it; "SCANNING n%" in Rajdhani, orange, outlined.
- Scanned rock (Asteroid._draw): the dashed ring became a glowing ring in the ore's colour with 6 turning nodes;
  the readout in Rajdhani.
- All sizes in screen pixels (same look at any zoom). CYAN is the GUI's cyan now; ORANGE added.
- Files: scripts/ship_scanner.gd, scripts/asteroid.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Fix: the exhaust plume failed to draw far out (signal sites)
- test_signals.test_stranded_and_under_attack failed now and then: "Invalid polygon data, triangulation failed"
  from ExhaustTrail._draw_glow. Signal sites are played at (240000, 240000); a small triangle in world
  coordinates that far out loses float precision in the renderer and degenerates.
- The plume (flame triangles and glow) is drawn round the nozzle (draw_set_transform) - small local coordinates.
  Also guarded: NeonBox skips the fill of a box too thin to triangulate; the scanner's sweep wedges need reach > 2.
- test_signals passes 4 runs in a row.
